title: Add grant-bound regeneration for existing generated work-package manifests
description:
Parent: Ligature port-feedback epic #143.
Blocks: release verification and downstream handoff #161.
Downstream project issue: full-ligature-port-workspace/date-creusot Chainlink #140.

Reproduced with Ligature 1.3.12 (source 34fb1a1372bd69e38a92f1468db6c4245a609518; bundle SHA-256 87ca4814b39def8f7f236f6c6a9be554992425112c339e22f0521e56c2e35028) in the date-creusot project at committed revision 729f0432c90dd7916bdbeecb750b9d5abbbbf5cd. Evidence: findings/limitations.jsonl entry date-ligature-103 and analysis/verification/creusot-0.14-2026-10-16.md.

Minimal repro: in a disposable copy containing the existing generated ci/manifest/WP-DATE-CREUSOT.json, issue an exact write grant for that path and run Stage 7 with a valid plan whose derived output differs (the captured probe used an eight-obligation plan to isolate replacement behavior; the live approved nine-obligation plan separately stops at date-creusot-063):
`python3 tools/ligature/ligature.pyz generate-work-package --plan <valid-plan-with-changed-derived-bytes> --issue 140 --toolchain rustc-1.90.0/cargo-creusot-0.14.0-dev/why3-1.8.2 --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu --grant-id <active-140-manifest-grant> --json`
Observed: exit 2, `target-conflict: ci/manifest/WP-DATE-CREUSOT.json already exists with different bytes; it was left untouched`. The live generated manifest remains unchanged and still directs assurance output to ci/results/feature_ledger.json, colliding with the feature-ledger projection.

Acceptance: provide a sanctioned, exact-path and issue-grant-bound update/regeneration flow for an existing generated manifest. Validate the full candidate (including current approved obligation scope, provenance and report.emit), then atomically replace the generated artifact and record auditable update provenance; on any refusal, preserve the old bytes. The canonical assurance output is ci/results/<work-package>.json, with the feature ledger separate. Verify either output can be regenerated while preserving the other. Do not permit silent scope widening/narrowing, hand edits, deletion, or a second package identity to bypass the guard.

comments.content: Implemented and released in Ligature 1.4.0. New generate-work-package --regenerate performs a grant-bound, atomic in-place update of this package's own existing generated work-package-manifest/1.0 after full candidate validation; hand-edited/foreign content is refused, the old bytes are preserved on every refusal, a grant cannot authorize a second change, and the audit event records result=regenerated with before/after hashes. Source and packaged-binary regressions added. Downstream manifest regeneration pending.

RESOLVED in Ligature 1.4.0 and verified downstream. generate-work-package --regenerate performs a grant-bound atomic in-place update of this package's own existing generated manifest after full candidate validation; hand-edited/foreign content and a second package identity are refused, the old bytes are preserved on every refusal, a grant cannot authorize a second change, and the audit records result=regenerated with before/after hashes. Downstream: the existing WP-DATE-CREUSOT.json was regenerated to the approved nine-obligation scope and canonical ci/results/WP-DATE-CREUSOT.json, and the feature-ledger projection and assurance report now coexist. Tests: tests/test_generate_work_package.py regeneration unit + packaged-binary coverage; docs/work-package-generation-audit-schema.json result enum extended.

Independent 1.4.0 review found that the hand-edit refusal criterion is not met. In a read-only in-memory probe, I loaded the current valid WP-DATE-CREUSOT manifest, changed report.emit to ci/results/manually-changed.json while preserving schema=work-package-manifest/1.0 and work_package=WP-DATE-CREUSOT, then passed those bytes to scripts/generate_work_package.py::_require_generated_manifest. The guard returned normally and accepted the changed bytes. It checks only JSON parse, schema id, and package id; it does not compare existing bytes to a previous successful work-package-generation audit after_hash. Therefore same-package hand-edited content can be overwritten by --regenerate under a fresh grant, contrary to this issue's stated acceptance. The live manifest was not edited: its SHA-256 is sha256:2adfab4a7d2c957ddc29d393c17b788630ccedb1a15a7d50fcd36cfe45bc61b2 and it matches the current audit event's after_hash. Please add an authenticated prior-generation/hash check (and a sanctioned adoption path if prior audit is absent), then test a modified otherwise-valid same-package manifest is refused with old bytes preserved. Reopening #164; its live output-path/coexistence workflow passes, but the broader regeneration-integrity acceptance remains incomplete.
